items.title: 'Like paradise': Women and children with IS-links excited to return to Australia
items.description: Australian authorities are preparing for the arrival of 13 women and children linked to Islamic State fighters, some of whom face possible arrest. Some are on a flight from Doha to Melbourne, while another flight is expected to land in Sydney. The federal government has always maintained that while it would not help the ISIS-linked families get home, it doesn't have the power to stop them.  ABC correspondent Bridget Rollason is on a flight and has spoken to some of the families.

items.title: Live: Energy giants to reserve gas for Australians from July under new gas policy
items.description: Energy giants will be forced to set aside gas for the domestic market from July next year, under the new east coast reservation scheme. Follow live.

items.title: Would you rather hand over $300 a month to your bank or the government?
items.description: As the average mortgage borrower confronts another $100 a month on top of their already inflated repayments, lots of people are asking if there is a better way to contain inflation than simply raising interest rates. It turns out there might be.

items.title: Jewish grandmother devastated by alleged fire attack on business
items.description: Grandmother Judith Lewis established Lewis's Continental Kitchen in 1970 alongside her husband, offering a kosher takeaway food option for the Jewish community, but it was destroyed in an alleged attack.

items.title: Live: Israel strikes Beirut for first time since Hezbollah ceasefire, Iran weighs up a peace deal
items.description: The strikes come as Iran weighs up a peace deal put forward by the US, with Donald Trump saying the war could "be at an end". Follow live.

items.title: This island was once ruled by Australia. Now, it could become the world's newest country
items.description: A tropical archipelago just 1,500 kilometres from Australia is readying to become the world's newest country. But as Bougainville nears independence, memories of a bloody past are coming back to the surface.

items.title: Is Richard Dawkins right about AI?
items.description: Is AI conscious? Richard Dawkins is asking the wrong question.

items.title: Kids throwing rocks at an Alice Springs riot should be a wake-up call to all of us
items.description: The riot in Alice Springs was yet another flashpoint for the small town trying to heal from heartbreak. So what does the future hold for Central Australia?

items.title: Breaking: Tens of thousands of Qld students affected in education software breach
items.description: Tens of thousands of Queensland students and teachers have been caught up in a major data breach, with names, school locations, and emails likely compromised.

items.title: Judge releases note purportedly penned in jail by Jeffrey Epstein
items.description: A note Jeffrey Epstein's cellmate claims he found after the convicted sex offender's first suspected attempt to take his own life in a New York jail has been made public.

items.title: One answer to Australia's housing affordability crisis is hidden in plain sight
items.description: What if the sudden improvement in Iain's life, and the extra $600 a month in his pocket, can be traced back to a single policy decision made by a federal minister in the 1980s?

items.title: The generation gap is real, but the 'bank of mum and dad' complicates it
items.description: Next week's budget will have the generation gap at its heart. But nailing down exactly what that gap is can be difficult. Here's what the evidence says.

items.title: Live: ASX opens higher, Tabcorp crashes on money laundering probe
items.description: The ASX's earlier gains are being trimmed as Tabcorp's shares are crunched on news of a fresh money laundering investigation. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Victorians wake to snow month out from ski season
items.description: Snow has fallen on Victoria's higher peaks overnight, as below-zero temperatures blast the state.

items.title: Can you identify Aussie movies from a single frame?
items.description: Think you know your Moulin Rouge from your Muriel's Wedding? Take our Australian movie quiz to prove you're the king of The Castle.

items.title: Explore Australia with these five great road trips
items.description: Whether you want to explore the red desert or picnic by a waterfall, an Aussie road trip awaits.

items.title: Trapped in an endless loop: Exit 8 and breaking free of doomscrolling
items.description: The creator of the minimalist horror film hopes it inspires viewers to stop doomscrolling and take a look at the world around them.

items.title: V8 nostalgia has hit F1, and a 'mega engine' could be the future
items.description: A bold vision of V8 engines has swept Formula 1, but the billions of dollars invested into hybrid technology means any view of the future must still consider electric power in one form or another.

items.title: Federation Square to host World Cup events after premier's intervention
items.description: Screenings of the FIFA World Cup will go ahead at Federation Square later this year after the Victorian premier overturned an unpopular decision to not host fans at the precinct.

items.title: Jane Fonda remembers CNN founder and ex-husband Ted Turner as 'swashbuckling pirate'
items.description: Turner revolutionised television news when he launched the world's first 24-hour news channel in 1980.

items.title: Preacher who wrote to terrorists while in jail refused parole
items.description: An Australian self-styled Islamic preacher jailed on drug charges will not be released on parole because of his extensive correspondence with convicted terrorists while in prison.

items.title: 'I'll show no mercy': Charity founder faces 'tickle torture' allegations
items.description: More victims of former Order of Australia recipient Cody Schaeffer have spoken to the ABC about his actions.

items.title: Passengers say 'ghost bookings' now common on crucial V/Line service
items.description: Public transport passengers in Victoria's north-west say a rise in "ghost bookings" has led to half-empty bus services during the state's free transport period.

items.title: Albanese's budget won't be derailed by Trump's pronouncements
items.description: It's clear that whatever this unpredictable US president says, the Albanese government isn't expecting a return to normal oil flows any time soon.

items.title: What will become of the Victoria Barracks? Communities have their say
items.description: Veteran, housing, heritage and community organisations are urging the government to put public needs first as dozens of defence sites get prepped for sale.
